summary: Tested the post-login launcher for owner@isodemo.com. Backend GET /api/staffing/me/portal-access returns {has_staff_portal:true, full_name:'Demo Owner'} correctly (200). Frontend: navigating directly to /launch renders the launcher page with all 3 expected cards (launch-staff, launch-operations, launch-service_desk) and clicking Operations navigates to /dashboard. TWO CRITICAL BUGS FOUND: (1) POST-LOGIN REDIRECT bypasses /launch — /login sends owner to /service-desk instead of /launch because LoginRedirectPage.js checks user.is_service_desk BEFORE the /launch fallback, and owner has is_service_desk=true. (2) STAFF PORTAL from launcher does not load — clicking launch-staff navigates to /staff-portal, StaffPortal.js calls /api/new-starter/me with the platform token which returns 404 'No onboarding case' (owner has a staff_members record linked but no onboarding_case), so StaffPortal falls back to /launch and staff-my-day never renders.

minor.issue: For linked staff_members (owner@isodemo.com) without an onboarding_case, returns 404 'No onboarding case'. Launcher's has_staff_portal=true criterion (based on staff_members) is inconsistent with StaffPortal's data source (new-starter/me requires onboarding_case). Either seed a case for the owner, or make StaffPortal render My Day from staff_members + staffing endpoints when the onboarding case is missing (activated employees don't need a new-starter case).

ui_bugs.issue: Owner (is_service_desk=true) is redirected to /service-desk on login, never reaching /launch, so the chooser is never shown. Task requires owner (Staff Portal + multiple modules) to see the launcher. The is_service_desk branch should not short-circuit users who also have Staff Portal + other modules; consider deferring to /launch when the user has 2+ destinations, or gating the is_service_desk branch on 'is_service_desk_only'.

Clicking launch-staff opens /staff-portal which calls /new-starter/me. Owner returns 404 → StaffPortal.js bounces back to /launch (usingPlatformToken branch). Result: launcher → Staff Portal card is broken end-to-end for owner. staff-my-day never renders. Either use /staffing/me/portal-access (already returns full_name) or a new /staff-portal/my-day endpoint that works without a new-starter case, or auto-create/backfill an onboarding_case on staff_members link.

integration_issues.issue: Full flow fails: launcher renders correctly at /launch, but launch-staff → /staff-portal → 404 on /new-starter/me → redirect back to /launch (loop). staff-my-day is never visible.
Signing in at /login with owner@isodemo.com lands on /service-desk, not /launch — the chooser is never presented.

action_items: CRITICAL: In LoginRedirectPage.js, do not short-circuit to /service-desk for users who have BOTH the Staff Portal AND additional modules — such users must land on /launch. Options: (a) call /api/staffing/me/portal-access before deciding the redirect, (b) always route through /launch and let LauncherPage decide (it already auto-redirects when only one destination), (c) only apply the is_service_desk shortcut when the user has no other module access AND no staff portal.

CRITICAL: Fix StaffPortal load path when user is a linked staff_member without an onboarding_case. Either (a) auto-provision an onboarding_case when staff_members is linked with active=true, (b) make /new-starter/me tolerant (return activated=true + person from staff_members when no case exists), or (c) point StaffPortal.js at a different bootstrap endpoint (e.g. /staffing/me + /staff-portal/my-day) for the platform-token flow.
Backend /api/staffing/me/portal-access is correct — no change needed.
critical_code_review_comments: LoginRedirectPage.js precedence — the is_service_desk shortcut runs before moduleHomePath()/'/launch', silently skipping the launcher for any user flagged as service desk. This is the ordering that breaks the new one-login → chooser flow.

LauncherPage.js is fine but relies on has_staff_portal being consistent with StaffPortal's bootstrap; today they read from different collections (staff_members vs onboarding_cases) → mismatch surfaces as a redirect loop.

StaffPortal.js catches ANY error on /new-starter/me and bounces to /launch — a 404 for a real staff member is treated the same as an auth failure. Consider distinguishing the two and rendering a fallback My Day.

rca of the issue: Bug 1 (missed launcher): In /app/frontend/src/pages/LoginRedirectPage.js the fallback chain is `is_master_admin → is_service_desk → is_partner_engineer → lite/pulse_pro → moduleHomePath()||'/launch'`. Owner has is_service_desk=true so the chain stops at /service-desk before ever considering the launcher. Reproduction: sign in at /login with owner@isodemo.com / IsoDemo123! — lands directly on /service-desk. Mitigation: move the /launch fallback in front of role-specific shortcuts when the user has multiple destinations, or make is_service_desk conditional on `!has_staff_portal && !has_other_modules`. Bug 2 (staff-portal loop): /app/frontend/src/pages/StaffPortal.js calls /api/new-starter/me which requires an onboarding_case (routes/staff_onboarding_wizard.py::recruit_me → _recruit_case). Owner has a staff_members record linked but no onboarding_case, so the endpoint returns 404 and the catch-block redirects platform-token users to /launch — infinite bounce. Reproduction: cd /app/backend && curl /api/staffing/me/portal-access → has_staff_portal:true, but /api/new-starter/me → 404 'No onboarding case'. Mitigation: either (a) auto-create an onboarding_case when a user is linked as a staff_member with active=true, (b) relax /new-starter/me to synthesize a minimal 'activated' response from staff_members when no case exists, or (c) replace the bootstrap call in StaffPortal.js with an endpoint that also works for already-active staff (e.g. /api/staff-portal/my-day).
